attribution_sensitivity.known_quirk: the literal single-token 'DRAGER' test would have flagged 15 Dräger strings / 108 events because the standard umlaut transliteration is 'Draeger', which does not contain 'DRAGER' as a substring. The implemented rule accepts both orthographies and treats every registry-accepted exact alias (including the 'Draeget' typo) as parent-attributed, so the net attribution removal is Medtronic only (Covidien/Tyco/Kendall/Valleylab era events). Strings that contain the parent token but belong to a since-divested line (e.g. 'Ge Healthcare, Breas Medical AB', 'Philips Lighting Co.') stay in pairs_no_acquired: the rule targets acquired-brand history, not divestitures.
attribution_sensitivity.rule: an event is removed when its company is one of the five deep cases and the upper-case applicant_raw is neither a registry-accepted exact alias of that company nor contains its parent-brand token (MEDTRONIC / GE / PHILIPS / DRAGER or DRAEGER / MINDRAY). The 48 auxiliary roster companies are unchanged: their brand-token sets are not audited (declared limitation).

history.reason: demonstrable exact-string defect: the registry omitted an FDA transcription typo of the Dräger legal name. The string is unique to Dräger and its 2 openFDA 510(k) device records (2004-06-02 and 2004-08-09; product codes CBK/CCK) had company_key = NULL, so they were silently dropped. Adding it is exact-string matching only (same treatment as the already-accepted Mindray typo "Bio-Meidcal"), not fuzzy or substring matching.

entity_resolution.scope: panel sources only (openfda_device_510k, openfda_device_pma); counts marked n_non_device_source_events cover the same applicant_raw string in the other store sources (recalls/ctgov/sec) for completeness but do not enter the panel
entity_resolution.store_mapping_note: the store company_key is a *current corporate group* mapping: historical events of acquired brands are attributed to the acquirer (e.g. Covidien/Tyco Healthcare/Valleylab/Kendall -> Medtronic). That is a point-in-time look-ahead in the entity definition; the pre-registration declares the auxiliary roster mapping unaudited. The deep-case audit below enumerates every such string; the panel variant pairs_no_acquired removes them.

left_censoring.definition: pairs whose first panel material event falls in the first four quarters of the grid (1976-Q1..1976-Q4); a pair that entered before 1976 is indistinguishable from a pair that never entered, so these are the pairs exposed to pre-1976 censoring

material_event_rule: material = every openfda_device_510k record; openfda_device_pma record only when payload.supplement_number is empty/null/'0'/'S0' or payload.supplement_type contains 'PANEL TRACK' (identical to experiments/reverse_rd_v2/run_v2.py)

grid_truncation.note: the store's PMA lane starts 1968-10-09: 22 PMA records predate the 1976-Q1 grid start and 18 of them are material (original approvals), but none is attributed to a panel company or track, so grid truncation costs the panel 0 events. 2026-Q3 is partial and excluded, which drops the 118 company+track-mapped material events dated 2026-07-01..2026-10-18; including them would give the counts shown above (these post-grid events can never be a label inside the 1976-Q1..2026-Q2 evaluation window, so no label information is lost).

track_coverage.note: 1958 product-code entries in config/product_code_tracks.json; the 7,097 figure is the row count of the store's product_codes table, not this file

product_code_fallback.note: the documented fallback (events.track_id missing -> product_code mapping) rescued no material event in this snapshot: every event without a track_id also has a product_code absent from the config file. The panel's effective track universe is therefore events.track_id only (38 of the 50 configured tracks).

track_coverage.scope: all material device events in the two panel sources, regardless of company
